correctness.rationale: Two fully specified isomorphic 28-vertex graph constructions were verified. Both exhaustive programs enumerate all 3,276 triples, none resolving, and all 20,475 quadruples, exactly 7,728 resolving. The C++17 program enumerates every exchange edge and breadth-first-searches the complete 7,728-node exchange graph from every node, checking all 29,857,128 unordered pairs and all numerical claims. The Python program separately rebuilds the graph from Fano nonlines, checks a 28-element isomorphism, verifies 336 distinct automorphisms, derives all 29 orbits, and independently rechecks eccentricities and detour counts by representative BFS. The exhibited two-move obstruction establishes nonmatroid behavior. Exact finite proof only; no sampled-to-infinite inference.

value.rationale: The Coxeter graph is a canonical symmetric cubic girth-seven graph with known metric dimension but previously unclassified full space of optimal sensor/landmark choices. An exact count of 7,728 optimizers and 29 symmetry orbits distinguishes genuine placement types; the 155,904-edge connected yet nonregular exchange graph, sharp Johnson-plus-one distance theorem, 449,820 forced detours and matroid-basis obstruction yield substantive structural information about reconfiguring optimal resolving locations rather than a routine recalculation of the scalar metric dimension.
